neighbours.label: Inside a person or place name that the tokenizer splits into pieces, the piece right after an opening 'Nir'/'Nar'/'Ner' or 'M'/'Am' chunk (Nir|upa, Nar|ita, Nari|ño, Ner|issa, M|ina, Am|ina); weaker after 'Sar'/'Har'/'Par' (Sar|ita, Har|ini). Patchy by spelling: many look-alike names stay quiet (Narges, Nuria, Norbu, Narendra, Lalitha, Karina), and the same letters inside ordinary words (margarita, senorita, nervous, nursery) stay quiet.
fire: Nirupa handed the keys to her neighbor before leaving for the airport.
We landed at Narita late in the evening and took the train into Tokyo.
The coffee farms of Nariño, in southern Colombia, are known for their bright flavor.
Nerissa laughed and said she had never seen the sea so calm.
Mina finished the crossword before anyone else at the table.
Amina is studying engineering at the university in Kano.
My aunt Sarita sends us mangoes every summer.
Harini played the violin solo at the school concert.
quiet: She handed the keys to her neighbor before leaving for the airport.
We landed at the airport late in the evening and took the train into Tokyo.
